mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 2.0%) consistently precedes positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as monetary easing reduces discount rates and boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 2.0% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 6.0%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Weak GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth < 0.5%) combined with declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) indicates economic contraction, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth < 0.5% and INDPRO < 100 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary easing cycles (FEDFUNDS declining and CPIAUCSL stable), the S&P 500 consistently generates positive 20-day returns due to reduced discount rates and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances during monetary easing cycles (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: A rising payroll employment (PAYEMS increasing in prior month) signals strengthening labor market conditions, leading to positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through higher consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 900 thousand (HOUST < 900) indicate a weakening real estate market, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced construction and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST < 900 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) are rising and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is falling, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns as consumer spending growth and monetary easing jointly support equity valuations.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong consumer demand
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS rises and FEDFUNDS falls (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: In industrial production contraction regimes (INDPRO declining), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative 5-day returns due to reduced manufacturing output and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances during industrial production contraction (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs 50%).
